messages:
support_ryan: Customer CB reporting build failures when fetching a private go module after they moved to a v2 tag. CI fails with a 401 from our GOPROXY. Repro steps below and a small go.mod snippet.

customer_cb: repro:
```
# clone their service
git clone git@github.com:customer/service.git
cd service
# go 1.20 in CI
cat go.mod
```

support_ryan: go.mod (redacted):
```
module github.com/customer/service

go 1.20

require (
    github.com/customer/pkg v2.0.0
)

replace github.com/customer/pkg => ../private/pkg
```

support_ryan: CI log: `go get github.com/customer/pkg@v2.0.0` -> `proxy.golang.org: 401 Unauthorized`

customer_cb: It works locally when I set `GOPRIVATE=github.com/customer/*`. CI uses our corporate GOPROXY which can't auth to fetch the tag. We only saw this after tagging v2.0.0.

eng_jess: Two likely issues: (1) upstream package's `module` path may not include `/v2` (Go modules require module path with major v2+), or (2) CI proxy/auth not allowing access to private tags. Can you run `go env` and `go list -m -json github.com/customer/pkg@v2.0.0`? Also try `GOPROXY=direct GOPRIVATE=github.com/customer/* go get github.com/customer/pkg@v2.0.0` as a quick check.

support_ryan: Ran `go list -m -json github.com/customer/pkg@v2.0.0` in CI container (redacted):
```
{
  "Path": "github.com/customer/pkg",
  "Version": "v2.0.0",
  "Info": "https://proxy.golang.org/github.com/customer/pkg/@v/v2.0.0.info",
  "GoMod": "https://proxy.golang.org/github.com/customer/pkg/@v/v2.0.0.mod",
  "Error": "403/401 from proxy"
}
```

eng_nick: If the upstream module's `go.mod` still says `module github.com/customer/pkg` (no `/v2`) and they tagged v2.0.0, `go` will expect module path `github.com/customer/pkg/v2`. The replace to a local path can hide that locally, but when CI tries to `go get` the tagged release the proxy enforces module path rules and/or fails auth. Two mitigation options:
- Ask upstream to update `module` line to `module github.com/customer/pkg/v2` and re-tag v2.0.0 (best fix).
- CI/workflow: set `GOPRIVATE=github.com/customer/*` and `GOPROXY=direct` so the proxy is bypassed and auth to git host is used.
- Temporary: vendor the dependency or use a `replace` in CI pointing to a commit URL that CI can access.

support_ryan: Example commands we suggested to customer:
```
# bypass proxy for this module
export GOPRIVATE=github.com/customer/*
GOPROXY=direct go get github.com/customer/pkg@v2.0.0
# or in CI runner
go env -w GOPRIVATE=github.com/customer
```

customer_cb: `GOPROXY=direct` fixed CI for now. But we need a permanent fix because our corporate proxy is required for other builds. We'll ask our internal infra team to add credentials for the githost to the proxy.

eng_jess: We'll also add a short note in our Go SDK upgrade guide about v2 module semantics and private repos + proxies. Escalating to eng-sdk to update examples and a troubleshooting blurb. If upstream can't/won't update their module path, the recommended long-term path is to re-tag or vendor.

deploy-bot: Ticket created REDWOOD-1234 (support -> eng-sdk) :ticket:

support_ryan: Closing loop with the customer for now; keeping ticket open. Will follow up once eng-sdk posts a docs patch or upstream fixes module path. :thumbsup:
